title: Improving SpGEMM Performance Through Matrix-Reordering and Cluster-wise Computation
problem: Sparse matrix-sparse matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) is bottlenecked by irregular memory access patterns and poor data reuse. Prior work on row-reordering mostly focuses on SpMV; SpGEMM-specific optimization is underdeveloped. Cache misses and low locality limit performance.
motivation: SpGEMM is fundamental to graph workloads and scientific simulations but achieves low performance relative to compute capability. Reordering schemes improve SpMV but don't directly apply to SpGEMM due to second-matrix access patterns.
method: The method reorders the rows of one matrix and organizes the other into hierarchical clusters (nested groups of data), which reduces irregular memory access and improves data reuse. A new row-clustered matrix format allows clustering to work independently from reordering. The researchers tested 10 reordering algorithms and 3 clustering patterns on 110 sparse matrices to identify the most effective combinations.
key_novelty: This is the first to systematically combine row reordering and hierarchical clustering for sparse matrix multiplication, introducing a row-clustered format that decouples the two techniques.
contributions: Hierarchical clustering framework for SpGEMM acceleration
Novel row-clustered matrix format and access pattern
Comprehensive evaluation of 10 reordering algorithms vs SpGEMM performance
Analysis of 3 clustering schemes on 110 matrices

findings.best_reordering: Graph partitioning provides best SpGEMM performance (high preprocessing cost)
findings.clustering_benefit: Provides better speedup than reordering alone at similar preprocessing cost

limitations: Abstract only - no architectural analysis, limited matrix type diversity details, no comparison with SpGEMM-specific prior work
primary_theme: Sparse matrix operation acceleration through reordering and clustering
